captions.linkedin:
Stop selling naked calls.

The Cboe built an entire index to show you the safer way, and it's been live since 2002.

It's called BXM. Whaley wrote the original paper in the Journal of Derivatives (2002). The mechanics:

🔹 OWN THE S&P 500 (the "covered" part, not naked)
🔹 SELL 1 AT-THE-MONEY CALL each month against full notional
🔹 ~50 DELTA strike, monthly roll cycle
🔹 Collect 1.69% to 1.8% monthly premium on average
🔹 Premium becomes a cushion in flat or declining tape
🔹 You cap upside above the strike. That's the trade.

32+ years of live, exchange-published data. No backtest curve-fit, no vendor screenshots. Just one of the oldest systematic income overlays in modern finance.

The retail mistake: selling premium without owning the underlying. Then one fast rally, account gone.

The institutional version: own the index, sell the call, sleep at night.

Strategy shared free. Performance depends on execution, sizing, and roll discipline, that's the part we engineer.

Here's what nobody tells retail option sellers.

The Cboe built an index in 2002 to track the safest, most boring version of "sell calls for income." It's called BXM, and the paper sits in the Journal of Derivatives (Whaley, 2002).

The mechanics, in plain English:

🔹 If the index rallies above your strike, you cap out. That's the cost.
🔹 If it drifts or drops, the premium cushions you.
